title: A limit that is a closed immersion is a closed immersion at a finite stage (closed-immersion transitions)
statement: Let $T$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Let $I$ be a nonempty directed set and $(Z_i)_{i\in I}$ an inverse system of schemes over $T$, with structure morphisms $h_i:Z_i\to T$, whose transition morphisms $Z_{i'}\to Z_i$ ($i'\ge i$) are closed immersions [def-weil-closed-immersion] (in particular affine [pqf-def-affine-morphism]), and let $Z=\varprojlim_iZ_i$ be its limit [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition], with $h:Z\to T$ the induced morphism. Assume every $Z_i$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, every $h_i$ is locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and $h$ is a closed immersion. Then $h_i$ is a closed immersion for some $i\in I$ (and hence, composing with the closed immersions $Z_{i'}\to Z_i$, for all $i'\ge i$).

source.place: Lemma Tag 0A0N (lemma-eventually-closed-immersion, line 956) and its proof (Lemma 09ZM eventually-affine, Morphisms Lemma 01QO closed-immersion)

proof.text: *Notation; reduction to $h_i$ affine.* Write $f_{i'i}:Z_{i'}\to Z_i$ ($i'\ge i$) for the transition morphisms, so $h_i\circ f_{i'i}=h_{i'}$, and $p_i:Z\to Z_i$ for the projections of the limit, so $h=h_i\circ p_i$ and $f_{i'i}\circ p_{i'}=p_i$. A closed immersion is affine [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-integral-separated-uc](b); hence the transition morphisms $f_{i'i}$ and the morphism $h$ are affine. $T$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated and every $Z_i$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated by hypothesis, so [lem-weil-pbc-eventually-affine] (Stacks 09ZM) gives $i_0\in I$ such that $h_i:Z_i\to T$ is affine for every $i\ge i_0$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0A0N (lemma-eventually-closed-immersion, line 956), proof, line 970: 'By Lemma 09ZM we may assume $X_i\to S$ is affine for all $i$'

proof.text: *A finite affine covering and the rings.* $T$ is a scheme, so covered by affine opens [def-pc-scheme], and quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]; choose affine opens $V_1,\dots,V_n$ with $T=V_1\cup\dots\cup V_n$ ($n=0$ if $T=\emptyset$), and put $R_j=\mathcal O_T(V_j)$. Fix $j$. For $i\ge i_0$ put $W_{j,i}=h_i^{-1}(V_j)\subseteq Z_i$, an affine open because $h_i$ is affine (step 1, [pqf-def-affine-morphism]), $A_{j,i}=\mathcal O_{Z_i}(W_{j,i})$ and $\varphi_{j,i}:R_j\to A_{j,i}$ the ring map induced by $h_i$; put $W_j=h^{-1}(V_j)\subseteq Z$, an affine open because $h$ is affine, $A_j=\mathcal O_Z(W_j)$ and $\varphi_j:R_j\to A_j$ the ring map induced by $h$. From $h_i\circ f_{i'i}=h_{i'}$ and $h_i\circ p_i=h$ we get $f_{i'i}^{-1}(W_{j,i})=W_{j,i'}$ and $p_i^{-1}(W_{j,i})=W_j$; let $\alpha_{i'i}:A_{j,i}\to A_{j,i'}$ ($i'\ge i\ge i_0$) and $\alpha_i:A_{j,i}\to A_j$ be the ring maps induced by $f_{i'i}$ and $p_i$. By functoriality of the maps on sections, $\alpha_{i''i'}\circ\alpha_{i'i}=\alpha_{i''i}$, $\alpha_{i'}\circ\alpha_{i'i}=\alpha_i$, $\alpha_{i'i}\circ\varphi_{j,i}=\varphi_{j,i'}$ and $\alpha_i\circ\varphi_{j,i}=\varphi_j$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0A0N (lemma-eventually-closed-immersion, line 956), proof, lines 971-973: 'Choose a finite affine open covering $S=\bigcup V_j$'

proof.text: *The three hypotheses of the affine case.* Fix $j$ and $i'\ge i\ge i_0$. (a) $\alpha_{i'i}$ is surjective: $f_{i'i}$ is a closed immersion, $W_{j,i}$ is an affine open of $Z_i$ and $f_{i'i}^{-1}(W_{j,i})=W_{j,i'}$, so [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-affine-cover-criterion](1) applies. (b) $\varphi_j:R_j\to A_j$ is surjective: $h$ is a closed immersion and $V_j$ is an affine open of $T$, so [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-affine-cover-criterion](1) applies. (c) $\varphi_{j,i}:R_j\to A_{j,i}$ is of finite type: $h_i$ is locally of finite type, $W_{j,i}$ and $V_j$ are affine opens and $h_i(W_{j,i})\subseteq V_j$, so [lem-weil-pbc-lft-affine-pairs] (Stacks 01T2) applies.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0A0N (lemma-eventually-closed-immersion, line 956), proof, lines 977-980: 'This reduces us to the affine case: $A=\colim A_i$ with $R\to A$ surjective and $A_i\to A_{i'}$ surjective for all $i\le i'$. Moreover $R\to A_i$ is of finite type'

proof.text: *$A_j$ is the colimit of the $A_{j,i}$.* Fix $j$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-limit-cone-affine-projections-opens](2) to the inverse system $(Z_i)$ (affine transition morphisms, step 1), its limit $Z$, the index $i_0$ and the open $W_{j,i_0}\subseteq Z_{i_0}$: the opens $f_{ii_0}^{-1}(W_{j,i_0})=W_{j,i}$ ($i\ge i_0$, step 2) with the restricted transition morphisms form an inverse system over the nonempty directed set $I_{\ge i_0}$, and $p_{i_0}^{-1}(W_{j,i_0})=W_j$ with the restricted projections is its limit in the category of schemes. All $W_{j,i}$ are affine, $W_{j,i}\cong\operatorname{Spec}A_{j,i}$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], so by [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition] (the clause from Stacks 01YW) this limit is also $\operatorname{Spec}(\varinjlim_{i\ge i_0}A_{j,i})$ (the colimit in commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]) with the projections induced by the coprojections. Two limits of one diagram are isomorphic by a unique isomorphism compatible with the projections; taking global sections ($\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}B)=B$), $A_j=\mathcal O_Z(W_j)$ with the maps $\alpha_i$ is a colimit of the directed system $(A_{j,i},\alpha_{i'i})_{i'\ge i\ge i_0}$ of commutative rings. For every $i\ge i_0$ the subset $I_{\ge i}$ is cofinal in $I_{\ge i_0}$, so $A_j$ with the $\alpha_{i'}$ ($i'\ge i$) is also a colimit of the restricted system over $I_{\ge i}$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0A0N (lemma-eventually-closed-immersion, line 956), proof, line 977: '$A=\colim A_i$' (the limit of the affine schemes $f_i^{-1}(V_j)$ is the spectrum of the colimit of their rings)

proof.text: *The affine case: $\varphi_{j,i}$ is surjective for large $i$.* Fix $j$. By step 3(c) choose $x_1,\dots,x_m\in A_{j,i_0}$ generating $A_{j,i_0}$ as an $R_j$-algebra via $\varphi_{j,i_0}$. By step 3(b) choose $r_k\in R_j$ with $\varphi_j(r_k)=\alpha_{i_0}(x_k)$ ($k=1,\dots,m$). Then $a_k=x_k-\varphi_{j,i_0}(r_k)\in A_{j,i_0}$ satisfies $\alpha_{i_0}(a_k)=\alpha_{i_0}(x_k)-\varphi_j(r_k)=0$ (step 2). Apply [lem-weil-pbc-directed-colimit-base-change-elementwise](2) to the directed system $(A_{j,i})_{i\ge i_0}$ with colimit $A_j$ (step 4), its index $i_0$ and the $A_{j,i_0}$-module $M_0=A_{j,i_0}$: here $M_i=A_{j,i}\otimes_{A_{j,i_0}}A_{j,i_0}\cong A_{j,i}$ by $a\otimes b\mapsto a\,\alpha_{ii_0}(b)$, under which $\mu_{ii_0}=\alpha_{ii_0}$ and $\mu_{i_0}=\alpha_{i_0}$; so there is $i'_k\ge i_0$ with $\alpha_{i'_ki_0}(a_k)=0$. As $I$ is directed choose $i_j\ge i'_1,\dots,i'_m$ (and $i_j\ge i_0$); then $\alpha_{i_ji_0}(a_k)=0$, i.e. $\alpha_{i_ji_0}(x_k)=\alpha_{i_ji_0}\varphi_{j,i_0}(r_k)=\varphi_{j,i_j}(r_k)$ for all $k$. The subring $\varphi_{j,i_j}(R_j)\subseteq A_{j,i_j}$ thus contains $\alpha_{i_ji_0}(\varphi_{j,i_0}(R_j))=\varphi_{j,i_j}(R_j)$ and the $\alpha_{i_ji_0}(x_k)$, which generate the subring $\alpha_{i_ji_0}(A_{j,i_0})$; so $\alpha_{i_ji_0}(A_{j,i_0})\subseteq\varphi_{j,i_j}(R_j)$. Since $\alpha_{i_ji_0}$ is surjective (step 3(a)), $\varphi_{j,i_j}$ is surjective. For $i\ge i_j$, $\varphi_{j,i}=\alpha_{ii_j}\circ\varphi_{j,i_j}$ is a composite of surjections (step 3(a)), hence surjective.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0A0N (lemma-eventually-closed-immersion, line 956), proof, lines 980-988: generators $x_1,\dots,x_m$ of $A_i$ over $R$, $r_j\mapsto x_j$ in $A$, an $i'\ge i$ where $r_j$ maps to the image of $x_j$, surjectivity of $A_i\to A_{i'}$

proof.text: *Conclusion.* As $I$ is directed and $n$ is finite, choose $i^*\in I$ with $i^*\ge i_0$ and $i^*\ge i_j$ for $j=1,\dots,n$ (any $i^*\ge i_0$ if $n=0$). Let $i\ge i^*$. For every $j$ the open $h_i^{-1}(V_j)=W_{j,i}$ is affine (step 2) and the induced ring map $\varphi_{j,i}:\mathcal O_T(V_j)\to\mathcal O_{Z_i}(h_i^{-1}(V_j))$ is surjective (step 5, as $i\ge i_j$). The $V_j$ are affine opens covering $T$, so $h_i$ is a closed immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-affine-cover-criterion](2). Hence $h_i$ is a closed immersion for every $i\ge i^*$, which is the assertion together with its parenthetical (equivalently, $h_{i'}=h_{i^*}\circ f_{i'i^*}$ is a composite of closed immersions).
